works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 1 in C minor
works.level_basis: AMEB Gr 4 set study (Series 8 edition: 'Largo-Allegro'; AMEB Gr 4 etudes average catalogue level 2); Music Analysis guide Level III; simplest bow-control study
works.contents: Largo sostenuto in C minor (four slow beats, full even forte tone, broad stroke at the point), then Allegro in C major on G7-based arpeggio figures; ends on the dominant (D) with a fermata, leading into No. 2. Winn: practise martelé at the point and Kreutzer 2 for the Largo; the Allegro is not possible at tempo with staccato bowing.
works.notes: Largo: even full tone at the point; Allegro: G7 arpeggio figures. AMEB Gr 4
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 2 in G minor
works.level_basis: No syllabus placement found; early in the book (Sieber title: 'd'une difficulté graduelle'); Winn: long commentary on bow strokes and trills; estimate
works.contents: Maestoso in G minor: martial, forte; dotted rhythms and chords opening on a low G-D double stop; first notes full bow, crisp strokes at the point, broad legato bars, regular trills (also with the fourth finger), some position work; closes on a G major chord with fermata. Winn: played too mildly it loses its character.
works.notes: Martial Maestoso: full-bow and point strokes, chords, even trills
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 3 in C major
works.level_basis: RCM 8 etude (2021 book p. 82 and syllabus list: 'Caprice in C major'); RCM 8 etudes average catalogue level 4-5
works.contents: Allegro in C major: up-bow staccato runs and mixed staccato/legato up-bow strokes; the more brilliant arm-stroke staccato in the upper third of the bow with free wrist and forearm (Winn).
works.notes: Up-bow staccato runs; mixed staccato/legato up-bows; RCM 8
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars); RCM 2013/2021 title

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 4
works.level_basis: No syllabus placement found; double-stop thirds in scale patterns (cf. Mazas Op. 36 Book 1, L3); Winn: 'one of the most useful'; estimate
works.contents: Moderato: opens in C major with double-stop thirds, later two flats (B-flat major area) and closes on a chord before No. 5 (B-flat major); thirds and scale runs in thirds played with a free, broad, slightly detached stroke in the lower half of the bow (second-position fingering); Winn calls it one of the most useful studies in the book and cites Halir's scale-in-thirds method.
works.notes: Thirds and scale runs in thirds; broad détaché in the lower half
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Key not settled from the Kross scan (see note): opens in C major (no signature), later two flats, closes on a chord before No. 5 in B-flat

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 5 in B-flat major
works.level_basis: RCM 8 etude (2013 book 'Caprice in B-flat major, Op. 3 No. 5'; 2021 list: one of 5, 6, 16, 28)
works.contents: Allegretto 6/8 in B-flat major: bowing study; Winn introduces systematic varied bowings here (Ševčík Op. 2 Part 2, Section IV), practising slurred and single bows at point, middle and heel.
works.notes: 6/8 bowing study: slurred and separate bowings at point, middle, heel
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars); RCM 2013/2021 title

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 6 in E-flat major
works.level_basis: RCM 8 etude (2013 book 'Caprice in E-flat major, Op. 3 No. 6'; 2021 list); Music Analysis exam guide Level IV
works.contents: Andante sciolto 2/4 in E-flat major: light cut strokes in the middle and upper half of the bow, accented trills, short point staccato versus broader détaché, careful intonation, raised-bow strokes in the middle (Winn).
works.notes: Light detached strokes, accented trills; staccato versus détaché
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars); RCM 2013/2021 title

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 7 in G minor
works.level_basis: RCM 9 etude list (2021: one of 7, 21, 22, 31, 32); Winn: 'not difficult' technically, so the low end of RCM 9
works.contents: Poco adagio con espressione, then Allegretto (2/4, G minor, closing on low G with fermata): expressive cantabile with ornamental turns and embellishments; tone colour, crescendo within phrases, vibrato. Winn: not difficult, but it demands tone colour and style (compare Mozart's adagios).
works.notes: Expressive adagio with embellishments; tone colour and vibrato
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 8 in G minor
works.level_basis: No syllabus placement found; slow cantabile study with modest left-hand demands (Winn); estimate
works.contents: Largo espressivo in G minor: stately sustained cantabile with dotted rhythms; shading, crescendo and diminuendo, vibrato, whole-bow strokes, a crescendo note in 4th position; Winn: one of the most artistic studies, similar in character to the Largo of No. 1 (count eight).
works.notes: Stately Largo: shading, swells, vibrato, whole bows
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 9 in G major
works.level_basis: No syllabus placement found; moderate arpeggio/string-crossing study early in the book; estimate
works.contents: Allegro in G major: arpeggio figures with a free forearm stroke in the upper half or third of the bow; string transfers on the edge of the hair (long transfers from the shoulder); scale runs started from the top note (Halir) (Winn).
works.notes: Arpeggio Allegro: free upper-half forearm stroke, string crossings
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 10 in D major
works.level_basis: No syllabus placement found; shifting to 5th position at speed; estimate
works.contents: Allegro in D major, forte in the upper part of the bow (similar in style to No. 9): changes between 3rd and 5th position with the first finger kept in place (Halir exercises); ends on the dominant (A) leading into No. 11.
works.notes: Forte upper-bow Allegro; 3rd-5th position shifts, first finger kept down
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 11 in D major
works.level_basis: Music Analysis exam guide Level V (AMEB Gr 7-8 range); no other placement found
works.contents: Moderato in D major: forearm stroke at or near the point; accented trills without disturbing the evenness of the notes; reading a whole measure at a glance and setting the fingers together; free elbow joint (Winn).
works.notes: Forearm stroke near the point; even accented trills; fingers set ahead
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 12
works.level_basis: Music Analysis exam guide Level V; Winn gives it his longest early commentary; no syllabus placement; estimate
works.contents: Moderato 4/4, written without key signature and modulating freely (opens on a repeated D-major arpeggio figure, closes on an E-flat trill figure): wide-ranging arpeggio and chromatic passages. Winn prefaces it with general remarks on how the studies are taken (individually, not in order) and on the French and German schools.
works.notes: Modulating arpeggio/chromatic study, no key signature; wide-ranging shifts
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Key not settled from the Kross scan (see note): no signature; opens on a D-major arpeggio, ends on an E-flat trill figure

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 13 in B-flat major
works.level_basis: Music Analysis exam guide Level V; two contrasting sections; no syllabus placement; estimate
works.contents: Andante 3/8 in B-flat major (2 flats), then Presto 3/8 (3 flats): smooth legato Andante with portamento on position changes (3rd to 1st), phrasing in two-note groups with accent and slight pause; light fast Presto. Winn: French graceful style with added dignity.
works.notes: Legato Andante with portamento and phrasing, then a light Presto
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan: Andante on 2 flats opening on B-flat-D-F figures; Presto on 3 flats

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 14 in C minor
works.level_basis: RCM 8 etude (2021 book p. 83 and syllabus list; original key C minor also accepted)
works.contents: Adagio sostenuto 'on the G string' (C minor; RCM title 'Cantabile una corda'): sustained cantabile on the G string alone; nobility of tone and tone colour; the Kross footnote compares the G string with the French horn and warns the strokes must not be executed too quickly.
works.notes: Cantabile on the G string alone: tone colour, nobility of tone
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars); RCM 2013/2021 title

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 15 in G minor
works.level_basis: Music Analysis exam guide Level IV; no syllabus placement; estimate
works.contents: Allegro in G minor: string-transfer patterns across two and three strings; Winn recommends Ševčík Op. 2 Part 2 Sections III-IV (two- and three-string transfers) and Halir's legato studies, with the left hand anticipating the bow arm.
works.notes: String-crossing Allegro (2-3 strings); Winn: Ševčík Op. 2 Part 2 transfers
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 16 in A minor
works.level_basis: RCM 8 etude (2021 list: one of 5, 6, 16, 28)
works.contents: Allegro moderato in A minor: a note followed by a sharply accented slurred group of three at the point of the bow, forte throughout; longer staccato groups at the point using little bow; the modulations make it a candidate for memorising (Winn).
works.notes: Accented slur-plus-staccato groups at the point; modulations
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan: no key signature; A-C-E arpeggios with G-sharp

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 17 in G major
works.level_basis: Music Analysis exam guide Level V; Winn: usually taken out of order for difficulty; estimate
works.contents: Adagio 2/4 in G major: cantabile in double stops and chords (opens on a B-D dyad); fingers placed simultaneously, slurs within slurs, whole-bow phrasing; leads into No. 18. Winn: one of the most interesting adagio studies, usually taken out of order because of its difficulty.
works.notes: Cantabile double stops and chords; fingers placed together
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 18 in G major
works.level_basis: Winn: 'unexcelled' double-stop study, positions to be mastered first; no syllabus placement; estimate
works.contents: Allegretto in G major: running double stops (Winn compares it with Kreutzer 12, 'may be played for years'); fingers placed together, lower-half raised strokes or a smooth running stroke in the upper half; positions must be known first; not to be played fast.
works.notes: Running double stops (cf. Kreutzer 12); fingers placed together
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 19 in G minor
works.level_basis: No syllabus placement found; spiccato/staccato bowing study; estimate
works.contents: Allegretto 2/4 in G minor (a later section on F-sharps): light spiccato at the middle of the bow, a broader stroke with the crescendi, tied notes alternately long and short in the upper third, staccato runs at the point (Winn).
works.notes: Light spiccato at the middle; broader strokes in crescendi; point staccato
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 20 in A major
works.level_basis: No syllabus placement found; four-string arpeggio crossings in high positions; estimate
works.contents: Moderato in A major (a middle section without key signature): string transfers in the positions on two to four strings, light running legato at the point, reading ahead, whole arm in one plane with the wrist leading; Winn: 'unexcelled' and a preparation for the finale of Bach's A minor Concerto.
works.notes: Arpeggio string transfers over 2-4 strings in positions; light legato at the point
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 21 in A major
works.level_basis: RCM 9 etude list (2021: one of 7, 21, 22, 31, 32)
works.contents: Moderato in A major (later chromatic passages): light legato bowing near the point; varied bowings suggested in several editions; position changes beyond the 3rd (flat thumb in 5th position); careful intonation at key changes (Winn).
works.notes: Light legato at the point, 5th-position shifts, intonation at key changes
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 22 in A minor
works.level_basis: RCM 9 etude list (2021: one of 7, 21, 22, 31, 32); opens in 7th position
works.contents: Adagio 3/4 in A minor (no key signature; opens on a high A in 7th position on the A string, later 6th and 3rd; closes on a chain of trills and a low A with fermata): cantabile in the upper positions; swells (crescendo/diminuendo), free vibrato, 'thinking' the first pitch. Winn: one of the most beautiful adagio studies, useful for Bach's sonatas and Spohr's duos.
works.notes: Adagio in 7th position: swells, vibrato, intonation; Bach/Spohr preparation
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan: no key signature; opens and closes on A (G-sharp accidentals)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 23
works.level_basis: No syllabus placement found; string-crossing study in the second half of the book; estimate
works.contents: Allegro 3/4, no key signature (opens on A-E-A arpeggio figures, closes over a repeated G pedal on a two-note chord; A minor versus C major not settled): two- and three-string transfers with slurred groups and a free (not staccato) up-bow; undulating wrist with slight arm movement; fingers placed quickly and held (Winn: the bowing is one of the most frequent in concertos).
works.notes: Two- and three-string crossings with slurs; free up-bow; quick finger placement
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Key not settled from the Kross scan (see note): no signature; opens A-E-A, closes over a G pedal on a two-note chord (A minor or C major)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 24 in A major
works.level_basis: No syllabus placement found; tenths and octaves with staccato (Winn); hardest of Nos. 1-28; estimate
works.contents: Allegro in A major (C time): short staccato; position work led by the fourth finger; double stops, octaves and tenths (tenths light, near the point, about three inches of bow), relaxed wrist; Winn: do not play it allegro if unprepared for the tempo.
works.notes: Short staccato, 4th-finger shifts; double stops, octaves and tenths
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 25 in C major
works.level_basis: No syllabus placement found; G-string cantabile with high positions; estimate
works.contents: Andante 3/8 on the G string ('4e corde', no key signature, C major: closes on C): singing legato with the theme returning on the E string; high positions (8va passages); a broad, not spiccato, up-bow staccato; sixteenths in the middle third, thirty-seconds nearer the point (Winn: an excellent example of phrasing and style).
works.notes: Singing Andante on the G string; high positions; broad up-bow staccato
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan: no key signature; G-string Andante closing on C

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 26
works.level_basis: Music Analysis exam guide Level V; no syllabus placement; estimate
works.contents: Allegro 3/4, marked 'f martelé', upper third of the bow, no key signature (A-centred, with G-sharps and C-sharps; ends on a two-note chord with fermata): crisp bright staccato contrasted with legato; free wrist and forearm. Winn: Fiorillo makes decided contrasts, and this one is more lively.
works.notes: Martelé and staccato in the upper third contrasted with legato
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Key not settled from the Kross scan (see note): no signature; A-centred with G-sharps and C-sharps, minor or major not clear

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 27 in D minor
works.level_basis: Music Analysis exam guide Level V; no syllabus placement; estimate
works.contents: Allegretto 2/4 in D minor (1 flat; opens on a D-F-A figure, later a D major section on two sharps; ends on A with fermata, leading into No. 28): groups of three notes with a light staccato first note over two strings; light stroke in the upper third or half; second position taken at once; fourth finger not released (Winn).
works.notes: Light staccato groups of three over two strings; second-position placement
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan: 1 flat, opens on D-F-A figures, later 2 sharps, closes on A with fermata

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 28 in D major
works.level_basis: RCM 8 etude (2021 list: one of 5, 6, 16, 28); Music Analysis exam guide Level V
works.contents: Allegro assai 2/4 in D major ('with the middle'): running light legato at or near the point with the bow over two strings; Winn: analyse each measure, introduce chords, play groups in twos, fours and eights or a flying staccato; return to Sitt double stops if the bow arm is not free.
works.notes: Running legato over two strings at the point; Winn's group-bowing practice
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan (key signature, opening and closing bars)

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 29 in D minor
works.level_basis: Music Analysis exam guide Level V; no syllabus placement; estimate
works.contents: Grave sostenuto in D minor (1 flat; closes on the dominant) then Moderato 3/4 (no key signature, ends on D with fermata, leading into No. 30): the Grave is a two-voice theme over a double-stop accompaniment (pure legato theme, bow over two strings, notes falling together); the Moderato contrasts crisp staccato (French: at the point; German: about a third of the bow) with legato (Winn).
works.notes: Grave: melody over double-stop accompaniment; Moderato: staccato versus legato
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan: Grave on 1 flat with half cadence on A; Moderato without signature ends on D with fermata

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 30 in G major
works.level_basis: No syllabus placement found; very high positions with rapid shifts (Winn); estimate
works.contents: Allegro 3/4, without key signature (G-major arpeggios, F-sharps as accidentals): short staccato in the upper third or martelé in the middle of the bow; crossing a string without sounding it; very high positions and rapid changes (8va passages); Winn: prepare with Schradieck and Ševčík.
works.notes: Short staccato/martelé arpeggios; string skipping; rapid high-position shifts
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan: no key signature; G-major arpeggios open and close it

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 31 in G major
works.level_basis: RCM 9 etude list (2021: one of 7, 21, 22, 31, 32); Music Analysis exam guide Level V
works.contents: Moderato 3/4 in G major (no key signature; starts in 2nd position on a G-B-D figure): varied-bowing study: flying staccato in the lower third, middle spiccato, legato in the upper third, one measure per bow, groups of four, running legato at the point; Winn: technically less difficult than some earlier studies; compare the bowings in Rode's 8th Concerto.
works.notes: Varied bowings: flying staccato, spiccato, running legato; cf. Rode's 8th Concerto
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan: no key signature; G-B-D figures; closes on a three-note chord with fermata

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 32 in E-flat major
works.level_basis: RCM 9 etude list (2021); Texas All-State Orchestra 2022-23 violin etude (quarter = 54-66)
works.contents: Adagio espressivo sostenuto in E-flat major (ends on the dominant B-flat with fermata, leading into No. 33): a singing melody over a clear, smooth lower-voice accompaniment that must be strictly in time (as in Bach's solo sonatas, Paganini and Viotti's 22nd Concerto); a running (not crisp) staccato run in line 3; Winn: musically superior to No. 33.
works.notes: Melody with strict lower-voice accompaniment (Bach-style); singing tone
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books
works.key_sources: Kross ed. scan: 3 flats, melody centred on E-flat, closes on B-flat (dominant) with fermata

works.author: Fiorillo, Federigo
works.title: Étude No. 33
works.level_basis: No syllabus placement found; arpeggios and octaves with 8va passages; estimate
works.contents: Allegro 3/4, no key signature (opens on a B-flat major arpeggio; closing key not settled): broad resonant arpeggio passages in the upper part of the bow, tone not decreasing on ascents, 2nd- and 4th-position work, octaves in the middle of the bow (slightly detached); Winn: review the arpeggios of Kreutzer 12.
works.notes: Broad arpeggios with singing tone; 2nd/4th positions; detached octaves
works.edition: Sieber, Paris ('oeuvre 3'; IMSLP dates the work c.1793); numbering and tempi as in the Kross ed. (Carl Fischer, 1900), Winn (1913) and the RCM books

Exams string: RCM 8 (mvt) and RCM 9 (mvt) are confirmed by the RCM 2021 syllabus (Level 8: Nos. 3 and 14 plus one of 5, 6, 16, 28; Level 9: one of 7, 21, 22, 31, 32); no Fiorillo at RCM 10/ARCT. AMEB Gr 4 is missing (Series 8 Grade 4 set study 'Largo-Allegro' = No. 1, per the Music Analysis guide; retailer lists (musicjunction.com.au) also show a Fiorillo study in the current Gr 4 and Gr 7 books); the Texas All-State orchestra 2022-23 list uses No. 32. AMEB Gr 6/8/CertPerf and ASTA CAP 8-10 could not be checked (AMEB site behind Cloudflare, ASTA CAP handbook members-only). note: FIORILLO: 36 studies reported as 36 individual works (set '36 Études or Caprices'); whole-book row id 617 already exists. NUMBERING: all numbers/tempi follow the Kross edition (Carl Fischer 1900, archive.org thirtysixetudeso00fior), which agrees with Winn 1913 (Gutenberg #65129), RCM 2013/2021 (Nos. 3, 5, 6, 14, 16, 28; 7, 21, 22, 31, 32) and the tempo lists of two complete recordings (Misciagna viola, Kino violin; Apple Music track lists). OPUS: IMSLP and the Sieber print say Op. 3 ('oeuvre 3'); the Goetz and Bachmann prints (and an archive.org scan titled 'oeuvre 4') say Op. 4; no opus is put in the titles for that reason. DATES: Fiorillo bapt. Brunswick 1 June 1755, d. after 1822/c.1823 (Winn says 1753). KEYS: read from the Kross scan (key signature plus opening and closing bars), checked against RCM titles; many studies end on a dominant or lead into the next one. Nos. 4, 12, 23, 26, 33 are left without a key in the title (confidence low): No. 4 opens in C major (thirds), moves to two flats and closes on a chord in that two-flat area just before No. 5 (B-flat major); No. 12 has no key signature, opens on a D-major arpeggio and ends on an E-flat trill; No. 23 opens on A-E-A figures but closes over a G pedal on a two-note chord (A minor vs C major); No. 26 has no signature, is A-centred with G-sharps and C-sharps (minor/major not clear); No. 33 opens on a B-flat arpeggio without signature and its closing chord could not be read. Nos. 22 (A minor), 27 (D minor, later D major) and 29 (D minor) are signature-less or modal readings from opening and closing notes (confidence medium). LEVELS: individual placements from RCM 8 (Nos. 3, 5, 6, 14, 16, 28 -> L4), RCM 9 (7, 21, 22, 31, 32 -> L5), AMEB Gr 4 (No. 1 -> L2), Music Analysis guide levels (No. 1 III; 6, 15 IV; 11-13, 17, 26-29, 31 V) and Winn's remarks; the rest are estimates (confidence 'medium'; the Music Analysis levels were confirmed on the product pages: No. 1 III, 6 and 15 IV, 11-13, 17, 26-29, 31 V). OTHER PUBLICATIONS: the IMSLP author category lists no other violin study or technique work by Fiorillo (the only other 'exercises' work is for harp, Op. 41); Winn's commentary and the arrangements/editions are in 'skipped'. Exam-board pages for AMEB and ASTA could not be opened.
